title: The CEO Who Posed as a Dead Man to Steal His Company's Pension Fund
hook: He faked his own death, assumed a corpse's identity, and drained a pension fund for 12 years before a parking ticket gave him away.
why_this_can_go_viral: The ultimate identity-swap crime feels like a thriller plot, triggering disbelief and morbid curiosity.

title: The Trader Who Used a Dead Satellite to Send Fake Market Signals
hook: He bought a decommissioned satellite, bounced false trade data off it, and caused a billion-dollar flash crash before anyone noticed.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines space tech with financial crime—a rare, high-tech heist that feels like science fiction.

title: The Startup That Sold 'Viral' Marketing—It Was a Botnet Hijacking Your Phone
hook: They promised exponential growth, but the 'audience' was actually millions of hijacked devices secretly sharing your ads at night.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exposes the dark side of 'growth hacking'—viewers will feel creeped out about their own devices.

title: The Monopoly That Bought All the Salt—Then Made You Pay $1,000 for a Bag
hook: They cornered the global salt market, created artificial scarcity, and watched governments beg while they raised prices 10,000%.
why_this_can_go_viral: Everyone uses salt—the idea of a single company controlling it triggers outrage and fascination.

title: The Spy Who Stole a Billion-Dollar Formula by Tasting the Rival's Product
hook: She was a 'flavor scientist' with a trained palate—one sip was enough to reverse-engineer the secret recipe and bankrupt the inventor.
why_this_can_go_viral: The superpower-like skill of tasting a formula once and stealing it feels like a heist movie.

title: The Ad That Used Your Camera to Guess When You're Sad—Then Sold You Booze
hook: Facial recognition analyzed micro-expressions during doomscrolling, triggering targeted liquor ads within seconds of a frown.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines surveillance capitalism with addiction—viewers will feel violated and share in outrage.

title: The Industry Cover-Up of a 'Biodegradable' Straw That Killed Sea Turtles
hook: The straws only broke down in industrial composters—which almost no one had—so they clogged oceans and gutted marine life for a decade.
why_this_can_go_viral: Greenwashing outrage combined with animal harm—emotionally charged and highly shareable.

title: The CEO Who Sold 'Cure-All' Water—It Was Tap Water With a Drop of Bleach
hook: He bottled municipal water, added a trace of bleach for 'purification', and sold it as a miracle cure for $200 a gallon.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exploits the wellness industry's dark side—outrage at vulnerable people being poisoned.

title: The Startup That Sold 'AI Childcare'—It Was a Webcam With a Minimum-Wage Watcher
hook: Parents paid $500 a month for 'AI safety monitoring' of their kids—but a human in a basement was just watching 15 screens at once.
why_this_can_go_viral: Taps into parents' fears and the AI hype bubble—relatable and terrifying.

title: The Monopoly That Bought All the Wood—Then Made IKEA Charge Double
hook: They secretly purchased entire forests and lumber futures, squeezing the supply chain until even the cheapest furniture doubled in price.
why_this_can_go_viral: Everyone buys furniture—the hidden monopoly angle feels like a conspiracy revealed.

title: The Ad That Used Your Typing Speed to Guess Your IQ—Then Sold You Loans
hook: Keyboard latency data revealed your cognitive processing speed—and predatory lenders targeted the slowest typists with high-interest offers.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exploits a seemingly harmless behavior—viewers will feel targeted and horrified.

title: The Factory That Sold 'Pure' Vanilla Extract—It Was Beaver Gland Secretions
hook: They used castoreum from beaver anal glands, labeled it 'natural vanilla', and sold it for 50 years before anyone tested it.
why_this_can_go_viral: Gross-out factor guaranteed—viewers will share it for the shock value alone.

title: The Industry Cover-Up of a 'Smoke-Free' Cigarette That Gave Off Cyanide
hook: The 'clean' cigarette produced cyanide gas when burning, and the company hid the lung-test results for 15 years.
why_this_can_go_viral: Taps into the long history of tobacco deception—combines health horror with corporate evil.

title: The CEO Who Created a 'Green' Energy Company—Then Dumped Toxic Waste at Night
hook: He marketed solar panels but secretly disposed of chemical runoff in rivers under cover of darkness for a decade.
why_this_can_go_viral: Hypocrisy at its worst—eco-friendly brand exposed as a polluter triggers moral outrage.

title: The Trader Who Used a Radioactive Leak to Crash Oil Futures
hook: He planted a small radioactive source near a pipeline sensor, triggered a fake leak alert, and shorted oil before the panic sell-off.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines nuclear fear with market chaos—high stakes and high drama.

title: The Startup That Sold 'Smart' Diapers That Listened to Baby's Cry—and Sold the Data
hook: The microphone analyzed crying patterns, but the real product was millions of hours of intimate home audio sold to insurance companies.
why_this_can_go_viral: Exploits the most vulnerable—babies—and turns intimacy into profit, triggering deep disgust.

title: The Monopoly That Bought All the Cement—Then Made Roads Collapse in a Year
hook: They deliberately used inferior limestone to cut costs, ensuring roads cracked within months—then charged governments to repair them.
why_this_can_go_viral: Everyone uses roads—the deliberate sabotage for profit feels like a villain origin story.

title: The Spy Who Stole a Drone Design by Posing as a Drone Racer for 3 Years
hook: He infiltrated the competitive drone racing scene, befriended the engineers, and walked off with blueprints for a military-grade prototype.
why_this_can_go_viral: Spycraft meets sports—a long con that feels like a Netflix thriller.

title: The Ad That Used Your Smart Speaker's Static to Map Your Emotions
hook: The speaker emitted inaudible ultrasound pulses that measured your heart rate, sweat, and breathing—then sold you antidepressants.
why_this_can_go_viral: Makes smart home devices feel like surveillance monsters—paranoia-inducing and highly shareable.

title: The Factory That Sold 'Organic' Beef—It Was Horse Meat Dyed With Beet Juice
hook: They used horsemeat from knackeries, dyed it red, and sold it as premium organic beef for 7 years until a DNA test exposed them.
why_this_can_go_viral: Gross-out and betrayal—a classic food fraud story with vivid, shareable imagery.

title: The Industry Cover-Up of a 'Safe' Microwave That Leaked Radiation Slowly
hook: The company knew the door seals degraded after 2 years, leaking cancer-causing microwaves—and buried the test results for decades.
why_this_can_go_viral: Everyone uses microwaves—the slow poison angle is deeply unsettling and practical.

title: The CEO Who Sold a City on a Fake Water Pipeline—Then Fled With $400M
hook: He pitched a desalination plant to a drought-stricken city, took the upfront payment, and vanished—leaving behind a hole in the desert.
why_this_can_go_viral: Classic con-man story with a massive scale—outrage at how easily cities are duped.
